(v) Fe, HCl, heating  →  product containing Fe
(vi) Co²⁺, CH₃COOH, excess KNO₂  →  product containing Co
(vii) CuSO₄, ZnS, froth flotation, activator  →  product containing Cu

Give the answer as an integer.

members.working:
Identify product containing named element for each reaction:
(i) Cu(OH)₂ on heating → CuO (black). CuO is paramagnetic (Cu²⁺ d⁹, S = 1/2).
(ii) FeSO₄ on strong heating → Fe₂O₃ (or Fe₃O₄). Fe³⁺ d⁵ high spin paramagnetic.
(iii) Cr³⁺ with H₂O₂, excess NaOH, warm → Cr(OH)₃ or CrO₃? Typically Cr³⁺ hydrolyzes to Cr(OH)₃, which is paramagnetic (Cr³⁺ d³, S = 3/2).
(iv) Cu²⁺ with excess KCN → K₂[Cu(CN)₄] (diamagnetic? Cu⁺ in cyanide complex often low spin d¹₀? Actually Cu(I) d¹⁰ diamagnetic; but product likely Cu(CN)₂ or complex with Cu⁺, diamagnetic. However typical KCN excess gives K₂[Cu(CN)₄] which is diamagnetic.
(v) Fe with HCl, heating → FeCl₂ or FeCl₃? Heating Fe with HCl gives FeCl₂ (if limited) or FeCl₃ (if excess). Both Fe²⁺ (d⁴) and Fe³⁺ (d³) are paramagnetic.
(vi) Co²⁺ with CH₃COOH, excess KNO₂ → Co(OH)₂ or Co(OH)₃? Likely Co(OH)₂ or Co(OH)₃, Co²⁺ d⁶ high spin paramagnetic, Co³⁺ d⁵ paramagnetic.
(vii) CuSO₄, ZnS, froth flotation, activator → CuS or Cu mineral? Typically CuS (sulfide) paramagnetic? Cu²⁺ in sulfide often low spin? Cu²⁺ d⁹ paramagnetic.
Thus only (iv) likely diamagnetic; others paramagnetic. Count paramagnetic reactions = 6.
Thus answer integer 6.
